expectations.evidence: Document only mentions NATO SECRET and COSMIC TOP SECRET (as out of scope). Does not list the full NATO classification hierarchy (NATO RESTRICTED, NATO CONFIDENTIAL, NATO SECRET, COSMIC TOP SECRET).
Line 101: 'NSM (Nasjonal Sikkerhetsmyndighet) | National Security Authority — accredits the facility and Norwegian national enclave'
Line 125: 'BSI (Bundesamt fur Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik) | Federal Office for Information Security — technical security standards'
Line 115: 'CFCS (Center for Cybersikkerhed) | National security authority for cyber — accredits Danish national enclave'

Lines 149-175: Four distinct classification domains with separate Norwegian, Danish, German enclaves and a shared NATO SECRET processing domain. Diagram shows physical separation with CDS layer between enclaves and shared tier.
Line 723: 'Crypto: NATO-approved cryptographic products' for shared NATO domain. Line 747: 'Shared NATO Domain | NCIA | NATO-approved crypto per AC/35'

Lines 190-194: Detailed CDS-mediated data flow rules between national enclaves and shared NATO domain. Section 10 dedicated to cross-domain data sharing architecture with content inspection and release authority.

Line 109: 'bilateral/multilateral security agreements must be in place.' Line 140: 'Bilateral security agreements (NO-DK, NO-DE, DK-DE) | Govern handling of each other's nationally-classified information'
Lines 533-539: Table shows personnel need both national clearance (e.g., Norwegian HEMMELIG) and NATO SECRET. E.g., 'Norwegian system administrators | Norwegian HEMMELIG + NATO SECRET'

Lines 788-793: Section 13.2 'Red/Black Separation' — 'Classified (red) and unclassified (black) signals must never share conductors, conduits, or cable trays' plus TEMPEST considerations throughout Section 13.

Line 95: 'NCIA accreditation requirements | System accreditation for NATO SECRET processing'. Line 720: 'Accreditation: NCIA or designated NATO accreditation authority'. Line 991: 'NCIA (or designated NATO authority) — for the shared NATO SECRET domain'

Lines 204-256: Section 5.1 details LIST-X equivalent facility requirements including perimeter security, access control zones, alarm systems, visitor control, TEMPEST zoning, and physical separation of domains with separate racks, cabling, and access control per room.
